record.paper_title: Several Open Problems on Banach Spaces (Castro Urdiales 2014)
record.context_brief: Direct sums of even Banach spaces
record.original_question: If X and Y are even real Banach spaces, must their direct sum X plus Y also be even without assuming that X and Y are totally incomparable? A real Banach space is even when it has complex structure but its hyperplanes do not.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Call a real Banach space $Z$ *even* if $Z$ admits a complex structure (i.e., there exists a bounded $\mathbb{R}$-linear operator $J\colon Z\to Z$ with $J^2=-\mathrm{Id}_Z$, equivalently $Z$ is $\mathbb{R}$-linearly isomorphic to a complex Banach space) but no closed hyperplane of $Z$ (i.e., no closed real-linear subspace of codimension $1$) admits a complex structure. Two real Banach spaces $X$ and $Y$ are *totally incomparable* if no infinite-dimensional closed subspace of $X$ is isomorphic to a closed subspace of $Y$.

Suppose $X$ and $Y$ are even real Banach spaces. Must the direct sum $X\oplus Y$ also be even, without assuming that $X$ and $Y$ are totally incomparable?
artifact.status_search_result: A web search surfaced related work by Ferenczi and collaborators on complex structures and totally incomparable Banach spaces, but no source explicitly resolves whether the direct sum of two even real Banach spaces must be even without a total-incomparability hypothesis. The status appears unresolved in the available literature.

status_evidence.snippet: Survey discussing complex structures, including Ferenczi's totally incomparable complex structures.
